"I don't care how many miles you've clocked on the pavement; if you can't handle the chatter on the gravel, you're going to fail."

I've spent the last six weeks training for my upcoming gravel race, and I've realized that my biggest mistake wasn't my lack of aerobic capacity. It was my inability to manage the vibration of the terrain.

I've shifted my focus from pure mileage to specific, high-intensity intervals that mimic the demands of gravel riding. I've been spending more time on unpaved surfaces, learning how to navigate the chatter and manage the vibration. I've also been working on my core strength, which is essential for maintaining stability on the gravel.

The lesson is clear: if you want to succeed in gravel racing, you can't just train like a road cyclist. You have to train specifically for the demands of the terrain. You have to learn how to manage the vibration, the chatter, and the instability of the gravel. Only then will you be able to truly compete.
